issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims the Eells–Sampson analogue for p.c.f. fractals (every continuous map to the circle is homotopic to a harmonic map) and that Strichartz's existence-and-uniqueness result is extended to p.c.f. sets. What is actually stated and argued is Theorem thm.pcf: existence only, with winding data prescribed on a cycle basis of a single graph Γ_m. The homotopy class of a map G→T contains winding numbers on loops at all scales, which this datum does not determine or control, and the Discussion concedes both points (no uniqueness is claimed, and classes with 'nonzero winding numbers at smaller scales' are not captured).

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed unique lift is not well posed: (lift-1) equates the real number f̄_γ(0) with the T-valued quantity f(0) without fixing a representative, so no integer constant is pinned down and uniqueness fails; (lift-2) evaluates f at x mod 1 ∈ T although f is defined on G (the lift in question is that of f_γ); and (lift-3), presented as a rewriting of (lift-2), asserts π∘f̄_γ = f̄_γ∘π, which is ill-typed (f̄_γ∘π is undefined) and should read π∘f̄_γ = f_γ∘π.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix a normalization for f̄_γ(0) (a representative of f_γ(0)) and correct (lift-2)–(lift-3) to f̄_γ(x)=f_γ(x mod 1)+k(x) and π∘f̄_γ=f_γ∘π.
issues.overall_effect: The degree ω(f_γ)=f̄_γ(1)−f̄_γ(0), Definition def.w-vector and the boundary conditions (bc-hm), which are all phrased through this lift, rest on an ill-posed object as written.
issues.title: The lift of f_γ is ill-defined and the lifting relation (lift-3) is wrong

issues.failure_explanation: tf(x)+(1−t)g(x) is meaningless for f(x),g(x)∈T: scaling a T-value by a real depends on the chosen representative. Reading the formula through lifts of f_γ and g_γ makes sense only one loop at a time; the displayed check (well-def) verifies only that a single parametrized loop closes up (using integrality of the degrees). Nothing shows that the values obtained from two different loops γ,γ′ that share an arc or a point agree, which requires the integer discrepancy of the two lifts of f along the overlap to equal the corresponding discrepancy for g; and uniform continuity of F on P×[0,1] is asserted without argument. Without these facts F is not a map at all and the density extension to G×[0,1] does not follow.

issues.failure_explanation: All three quantities in (bc-hm) are differences of values of the lift f̄_{γ_0}, and (homotopy-c) fixes only winding numbers; both data sets are invariant under f ↦ f+c mod 1 for any c∈T. Hence every solution f yields the distinct solutions f+c, contradicting the stated uniqueness. The construction itself fixes the translation artificially (f(v_1^0)=0 in (def-H)), and the paper states 'up to translations' for the analogous circle case.

For m≥2 the values at z_± are already fixed on V_{m−1}^0 and the standard compatibility is valid.

issues.failure_explanation: By (d-harm), Γ_m^0-harmonicity requires the discrete Laplace equation at every node of V_m^0∖V_0, which includes the cut vertices z_±^0. But f_m^0 minimizes over H_m^0, where the jump condition binds at z_±, so the Euler–Lagrange equation survives only for the sum of the variations at z_+ and z_−. With f|_{V_0}≡0, δ_1=δ_2=0, ρ_0=1, (Hext) gives f_{z_-}=−1/2, f_x=−1/10 and the Laplacian at z_- equals (f_{v_1}−f_{z_-})+(f_x−f_{z_-})=0.5+0.4≠0. The proof of Theorem lem.ext_harmonic_on_G confirms this by treating the equations at z_±^k as still to be proved.

issues.failure_explanation: E[Γ_m^0] is a sum of squares of real differences, whereas (Em-hat) sums unsquared geodesic distances; the displayed identity Ê_m(f̂*_m)=E[Γ_m^0](f*) is therefore false as written, and the minimization claim cannot hold for the functional actually defined (for the unsquared functional every monotone interpolation is a minimizer, so minimizers are non-unique, e.g. on a single edge with fixed endpoints). issues.failure_explanation: The loops γ_i were indexed by the words w in lexicographical order (so ∂T_{12} is γ_5), but (re-deg) assigns to w=(w_1,…,w_m) the index ℓ(w)=Σ_{i=1}^m w_i3^{i−1}=(3^m−1)/2+Σ_i(w_i−1)3^{i−1}, which orders the words of length m colexicographically (e.g. ℓ(12)=7 whereas γ_7=∂T_{21}). Since the cut made at ξ_w carries the jump ρ_{ℓ(w)}, the map produced has ω_{∂T_w}=ρ_{ℓ(w)}: its degree vector is a permutation of the prescribed one as soon as the entries differ, so 'the prescribed degree' is not realized.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ℓ by the lexicographic index ℓ(w)=(3^m−1)/2+Σ_{i=1}^m (w_i−1)3^{m−i}, or change the labelling convention to match the existing formula and update the statements referring to it.
issues.overall_effect: The higher-order algorithm of Section 7 and the Appendix does not deliver its stated input-output contract (a harmonic map with the prescribed degree vector), although it does deliver some harmonic map of the same combinatorial type.
issues.title: Index map ℓ conflicts with the lexicographic labelling, so the higher-order construction realizes a permuted degree
issues.why_classification: A local change of one index formula (or of the ordering convention) fixes the contract; the construction, its correctness argument and all guarantees are otherwise intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there is a non-trivial embedding of cycles from $\Gamma_m$ to $\Gamma_{m+1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: ω_γ(f) for γ∈Cyc(Γ_m) presupposes that the graph cycle is realized as a parametrized loop in K; for a general p.c.f. set an edge of Γ_m has no canonical realization and the text only says 'by abuse of notation γ_0 also stands for the corresponding loop in K' (and (pcf-bc-hm) even uses the undefined ω_p(f)). More seriously, the construction cuts at ξ(γ_i^{(m)})∈V(ι(γ_i^{(m)})) — a vertex of the EMBEDDED cycle at level m+1 — while the prescribed winding is around the level-m cycle γ_i^{(m)}. Conditions (cycle_extend)–(pcf-cut) compare only vertex sets of cycles at different levels; nothing ensures that ξ(γ_i^{(m)}) lies on the loop γ_i^{(m)}, nor that the other loops γ_j^{(m)} avoid ξ(γ_i^{(m)}) in the interior of an edge. The paper itself notes that for the pentagasket the embedding is 'non-trivial'. Hence the jumps need not produce ω_{γ_j^{(m)}}=ρ_j. (For the SG the analogous step works only because there the cut point is explicitly required to lie on ∂T_w∖∂T_{w′}.)

diagnostic_evidence.quote: results in a uniformly continuous function on $V_*$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof produces a harmonic function only on the dense set Ṽ_* and then 'extends by uniform continuity'. Uniform continuity of the discrete harmonic extensions is a property of the harmonic structure that is never assumed or proved: Section 8.1 postulates only self-similarity and compatibility (i.e. a harmonic structure), not its regularity. Without regularity the resistance metric need not be comparable to the Euclidean metric of K and the values produced by the harmonic extension algorithm need not be uniformly (or even Euclidean-) continuous, so the limit need not define a continuous map K→T. For the SG the paper cites a source for exactly this step; no analogue is provided in the general setting.

failure_location.quote: and further extended by uniform continuity to obtain a harmonic function on the entire $\tilde{K}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add regularity of the harmonic structure and invoke (or prove) that the harmonic extension is then uniformly continuous in the Euclidean metric, or restrict the theorem to harmonic structures for which this continuity is known.
issues.overall_effect: Without continuity the constructed object is not a map K→T, so the existence claim of Theorem thm.pcf is unsupported for the stated class of harmonic structures, and the abstract's extension to p.c.f. fractals with it.
issues.title: Theorem thm.pcf: continuity of the harmonic extension is assumed without the needed hypotheses
issues.why_classification: A standard extra hypothesis plus an appeal to existing continuity theory restores existence for all advertised examples; the proof architecture is unchanged, but the assumed class of harmonic structures shrinks.
